children: Supported by major new product launches, significant cost savings, and an earnings tailwind from LiveWire, Harley-Davidson
is poised for a meaningful improvement in retail sales, with Citi Research analyst James Hardiman seeing 2026 demand strength potentially marking the start of a “multi-year retail growth story.”
to Buy from Neutral and raises his profit estimates for the remaining two quarters of the year and out to 2028.

“The facts on the ground have changed enough to warrant a more constructive view,” Hardiman says of the motorcycle manufacturer. “What began as modest retail improvement in early 2026 now appears to be building.”
U.S. retail unit sales were up mid-to-high single digits in the third quarter, with September sales improving by double digits thanks to already strong months of July and August.
Boosting the bottom line is Harley-Davidson’s
Back to the Bricks plan, which aims to achieve more than $150M of fixed cost savings by 2027.
“Hence, a two-pronged demand and margin story would represent rarified air for Harley-Davidson,” Hardiman says.

Citi has been cautious on HOG for several years due to declining retail demand for more than a decade (with the exception of Covid-fueled demand in 2021), deteriorating dealer sentiment, bloated inventory, and questions surrounding the brand’s ability to return to sustainable growth given a “well-traveled secular/demographic bear case.”

But with demand gaining momentum, Hardiman believes HOG would be on pace to significantly outperform current expectations and exit 2026 with the strongest retail momentum in years. This can be attributed to healthier dealer inventories, improved dealer alignment, a broader product portfolio, and a more “normal demand environment.”
plans to revive the Sportster, a model dealers have repeatedly identified as one of the company’s biggest mistakes to discontinue.

“The planned return of a roughly $10,000 highly customizable Sportster should help fill a major gap in the lineup and re-establish a meaningful entry point into the brand,” Hardiman says, adding that even if the entry-level motorcycles contribute little profit on their own, they could provide enough retail momentum to support investor confidence in an earnings recovery that is being driven by cost reduction and operational improvements.

Along with an upgrade and 6% price target increase to $33, Hardiman raises his Q3 and Q4 EPS estimates by $0.10 and FY26 by $0.20 to $0.36, ($0.64), and $0.71, respectively, and moves FY27 EPS up $0.14 to $2.22 and FY28 by $0.30 to $3.11. This incorporates not only improved operating income but also a "dramatic reduction" in Livewire losses between now and 2028.
The new bullish outlook on Harley-Davidson
is lifting shares by more than 4% higher in Monday’s premarket trading.
